The final incident summary must use the official postmortem figures, not the informal engineering estimate of "about 20 customers." The correct figures are **17 affected customer workspaces** and **142 document upload requests failed or remained stuck in the indexing queue** [NL-013-S02]. 

**Why these figures belong in the final summary:** 
- The engineering estimate of "maybe around 20 customers" (from NL-022-S03) was explicitly an informal guess made during a status call before the audit was complete [NL-022-S03]. 
- The official postmortem, compiled later after a complete audit of database transaction logs, confirms that exactly 17 customer workspaces were directly affected [NL-013-S02]. This same audit identified the 142 failed/stuck document upload requests [NL-013-S02]. 
- The postmortem itself (NL-013-S09) establishes that the engineering standup guess ("maybe around 20 customers") caused confusion for Customer Success, and it expressly designates the postmortem database audit as the **sole authority** for customer-impact metrics (stating that publishing internal engineering guesses before audits are complete must be avoided) [NL-013-S09]. 

Therefore, the final summary should report 17 affected customer workspaces and 142 pending/failed documents, based on the authoritative database audit [NL-013-S02] and policy establishing the audit as definitive [NL-013-S09].
